core_obligations: Note that the intersection of the powers of I vanishes because that of J does, and reduce by the single-generator criterion to the case I = (f) (proof lines 23000-23004).

Given a compatible sequence modulo powers of f, use J-adic completeness to find a limit modulo the J-adic filtration, and reduce to the case where the sequence lies in the J-adic filtration (proof lines 23005-23009).
Use the telescoping relation x_n - x_{n+1} = f^n z_n to write each x_n as f^n times a convergent series, showing that the sequence converges f-adically (proof lines 23010-23019).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a principal ideal using the surjectivity criterion (proof lines 22999-23004).
Sum the telescoping series to get f-adic convergence (proof lines 23004-23020).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for ideals I contained in J with I finitely generated, every J-adically complete module is also I-adically complete (statement lines 22992-22997). The proof does not compare the two filtrations abstractly: it reduces to a principal ideal by the single-generator surjectivity criterion, uses J-adic completeness to find a limit, reduces to sequences lying deep in the J-adic filtration, and then exhibits each term as f^n times a convergent geometric-like series obtained from the telescoping relation (proof lines 22999-23020). Recognising the telescoping sum and proving its convergence is the substance, and the author writes the series out. H2.
